method: Reviewed the regression lesson against OpenAI evaluation best practices and the NIST proportion-interval reference. Executed the embedded example and ran five offline assertions for scenario arithmetic/transcript consistency and interval boundaries. No provider or external service calls were made.

observations.trace: For the fixed 30-case fixture, A repairs one and regresses one (net 86.7%), B repairs cases 3 and 11 with no regressions (93.3%, +6.7pp), and C repairs two and regresses two (net 86.7%). The 26/30 single-group normal-Wald 90% width is about 20.4 percentage points and is not used to adjudicate version differences.

limitations: The fixture is deterministic constructed data; no provider request, production CI execution, or randomized model evaluation was performed.
The review did not recover original historical prompts, responses, model/endpoint fingerprints, or run-by-run scorer outputs; it therefore does not validate historical model results.
The NIST interval reference supports the limitations of proportion intervals; it does not validate a version-comparison design or the missing historical data.
The CI workflow remains an illustrative snippet and was not run in a repository workflow.
